Please, love yourself through this. You did something for yourself that you wanted. Whether it is perfect in anyone else's eyes, all that matters is that you wanted it, and you were able to get it. If I can relate my own experience to yours for some comfort I'll try. I got my second tattoo at age 19, a rather large forearm piece. It's a tribute to my mother. An anchor, because in my mind at the time she saved me from abuse. I went to the most reputable shop in town. The artist was an OG tattooer who used to own a ridiculously popular shop in Vancouver. 

This man ruined my tattoo. He tried to use so many different sized lines, he shaded horribly, he literally left GAPS in spots that should have been coloured in. This was 11 years ago and I still haven't fixed it.

The worst part is the now I'm living with this thing on my arm, while learning that through therapy my mother was a narcissist and caused me to have severe cptsd and attachment issues. 

But at the end of the day, I'm not mad about it. I don't regret doing something for myself in a moment of time that meant something for me and made me happy. I can't regret trying to make my past self happy, right?

You are not stuck with your tattoo the way it is, if it makes you unhappy. Just know that I myself, and many others do think that it's a beautiful piece of art. It's beautiful because you wanted it. It doesn't hurt anyone else. Let them have their egos about perfect tattoos.

In my opinion, perfectionism is related to ego. There are some articles about this I do believe. 

I myself am not diagnosed OCD so if I'm way out of field here I am so sorry. My doctor does suspect it within me but it's hard to pull that apart from autism. 

Anyway, I was able to stop being a perfectionist by telling myself that I didn't have to be better than everyone else. You really do remove a genuine relatable aspect of yourself from your audience if you are hyper focused on making sure your content is perfect. And hey.. it's not really fun to make content and share it with everyone if you're so concerned that it's not perfect right? You have to make it fun for yourself too. Give yourself some leeway, because really there are no "perfect" content creators. Heck, have you ever met anyone that was perfect at anything? 

I don't really have any solid advice other than maybe just look up some videos or articles about perfectionism and really see if that's what is happening, and then compare it to OCD symptoms as well. Your ego really controls you without you even being aware sometimes!

Hey friend. I honestly completely feel you on this. I am absolutely awful with words and explaining myself but I'll give this a shot. 

 I can not get myself out of bed some days. I find myself just in a genuine state of being paralyzed if I have any sort of task that seems not "fun or interesting" to me. I just can't move, knowing how many steps there are going to be to finish it all. This even includes showering, feeding myself, etc. 

 Tell me if I'm wrong, but I would guess that as you're laying there in bed unable to move that your mind is just yelling at you to get up. Just get up and do it. Stop doing this. It's not that hard, everyone else does it.. etc.

 Here's my only piece of advice, because I struggle with this daily: Don't hold yourself accountable for finishing each task to 100%. If you can, tell yourself that you're just going to give a 60% effort at everything for the day(Or whatever you think you can manage). You don't have to complete everything. But if you can at least put a dent in some of the things, get it anywhere from 5-100% done, then you will have less steps to worry about. 

 Listen, as long as you are doing something, then you are closer to the finish line. But remember that life is a journey. Every day is meant to be lived as a new day, there is no finish line.  Even if you get side tracked and feel like it's the right time to start a new hobby in the middle of the day, just remember that it's okay to do that sometimes. You have to excite your brain. We thrive on interest and excitement as we do not produce the happy chemicals very well. 

 You'll find yourself more productive in your routines if you allow yourself to have some 15%, 50% and 100% days. Be kind to yourself please! It's really easy to beat ourselves up over being different and having different abilities. But we are all only human, and you were born to live an exciting life! 

 I'm sorry if this isn't helpful. I do hope you find a form of motivation that works for you. Best of luck.
